# ===========================================================================
# THE GATE.
#
# EVERY `py=` LITERAL BELOW IS A ROW OF `.agents/slop/ga-oracle.txt`, WHICH
# CALLS generate.py's OWN FUNCTIONS -- `_strip_enc`, `_norm_field`,
# `_map_flat`, and the four emitters, whose emitted FILES are read back.  No
# `py=` here was typed by a human; `.agents/slop/ga_fix.py` splices them in
# from the oracle, and it REFUSES to emit a row whose name is not in the
# oracle file.  That is the rule five files in this project broke by hand
# (`cstyle` 17/215, `ops_nv` 33/219, `rdma` one hex digit, `amdev` 7/80,
# `ops_qcom` one table entry).
# ===========================================================================

def g(nm: String, got: String, want: String) -> IO(Unit):
  IO.print(String.concat([nm, " = [", got, "]   py=[", want, "]"]))

# THE EMITTER ROWS ARE ONE ROW PER EMITTED LINE, `nm | <index>`, PLUS `nm lines`.
#
# A count row alone would be identical for a dropped member, a dropped alias, a
# swapped `default=NULL` and a reordered field; the 634 line rows are what see
# those, and they are the renderer convention 2 applied to a GENERATOR: the
# answer is the FILE, one line at a time.
#
# AND IT MUST BE PER LINE, MEASURED TWICE OVER.  The row parser splits lane
# output on newlines, so one whole-file row became 335 fragments whose NAMES
# are the first token before an `=` inside the generated Python: 233 row names
# for 91 rows, 84 shared with the oracle, the other 149 naming text the oracle
# calls `tag | line`.  The fix `cstyle.bend:1760` writes down for this --
# `esc_row`, a newline turned into a backslash and an `n` -- FAILS TWICE OVER
# HERE.  `String.split` is one frame per CHARACTER (base.bend:2009) and the file
# is 16,815 characters; and even handed the lines as a list, `String.join` is
# O(total length) in stack depth, because base.bend:1980 appends onto a growing
# prefix (base.bend:1806).  Probe: 177 lines of 95 characters, 6 of 6 through
# `String.concat`, and on the real file 10 of 20 through either join.  THE
# ORIGINAL, ONE WHOLE-FILE ROW AND NO ESCAPE AT ALL, WAS 5 OF 12 -- so the flake
# predates this change and no lane on this port was reliably runnable.
#
# A per-line row builds no string longer than one emitted line, so it cannot
# reach that ceiling, and it needs no escaping at all -- which also retires
# cstyle's escape ambiguity outright.  That ambiguity is a real concern here:
# `write_pcode` emits `{code!r}` (generate.py:497), so CPython's OWN output holds
# a literal backslash-n inside a pcode body, and an escaping gate cannot tell it
# from a line break.
#
# `want` IS A LIST, NOT ONE STRING, and that is measured too: walking `want`
# with `String.take`/`String.drop` (base.bend:1932/1941) recurses over the prefix
# it consumes, so one 177-line file was 9 of 12 while the same 177 rows over two
# list arguments were 20 of 20.  `write_*` RETURNS a list (generate.py:276-282,
# :457, :469, :494), so the expectation is written in the shape the function
# already has and the two sides are walked in lockstep.
#
# `lines` IS NOT A COVERAGE CLAIM.  It is the one hole the index opens: an index
# cannot see a dropped LAST line.  `wc` is CPython's count and the port's is its
# own list length, so they are two numbers from two places.  The LENGTH MISMATCH
# arm is a loud stop, not a row: it prints a name no oracle row carries, so it
# cannot be mistaken for agreement.
def gl.go(+nm: String, got: List<&2, String>, want: List<&2, String>, wc: String, +i: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match got, want:
    case Nil{}, Nil{}:
      g(String.concat([nm, " lines"]), U32.show(U32.from_nat(i)), wc)
    case +h <> t, +wh <> wr:
      do IO<Unit>:
      g(String.concat([nm, " | ", U32.show(U32.from_nat(i))]), h, wh)
      gl.go(nm, t, wr, wc, Nat.add(i, 1n))
    case _, _: IO.print("LENGTH MISMATCH -- the port and CPython emitted a different NUMBER of lines")

def gl(nm: String, got: List<&2, String>, want: List<&2, String>, wc: String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
  gl.go(nm, got, want, wc, 0n)
